verdict.headline: SK Hynix's record quarter lifts chip stocks again before the Fed and Microsoft, Alphabet results
verdict.label: Pre-market: Nasdaq-100 futures +0.41%, S&P 500 futures +0.1%, Dow futures -0.17%; 10Y 5.013%; Brent $114.87; DXY 102.42; BTC ~$80,850.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: SK Hynix reported a record 83.3 trillion won of third-quarter operating profit against a consensus near 77 trillion and said memory demand should exceed supply through 2030. Nasdaq-100 futures rose 0.41% and Micron about 4% before the open, and the Kospi closed up 6.8%. The 10-year rose back above 5% to 5.013% and Brent gained 0.87% to $114.87 on Houthi attacks and US threats toward Iran.

What it means: Tuesday's chip rally rested mostly on suppliers financing their customers; SK Hynix supplies the demand evidence that was missing. Rates have not eased with it, though. A December hike is still priced at 76.5% going into today's Fed decision, and NXP fell 8.5% on a guide that only matched forecasts, so chip results still need to beat.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back under 26,424.82 after Microsoft and Alphabet report tonight would return the index to its range, and under 26,169.38 would erase this week's gain. A 10-year above 5.11% after Chair Warsh's press conference would put rates back in charge of tech.
verdict.lede_short: SK Hynix's record profit and its call that memory stays short through 2030 have Nasdaq futures up 0.41% before the open, giving Tuesday's financing-led chip rally a demand number. Rates have not followed: the 10-year is back above 5% and a December hike is still 76.5% priced into today's Fed decision. Microsoft and Alphabet tonight decide whether the Nasdaq holds above 26,424.82.

supporting_data.label: SK Hynix's third-quarter operating profit rose 632% to a record 83.3 trillion won and its shares closed about 10.9% higher — the largest memory supplier to Nvidia is reporting demand, not financing, behind the chip rally.
Nasdaq-100 futures rose 0.41% and Micron about 4% before the open while Dow futures fell 0.17% — the buying is again concentrated in memory and chips rather than spread across the market.
Fed funds futures price a 90.6% chance of a hold today and 76.5% for a December hike — the decision matters only for what Chair Warsh says about December.

Brent rose 0.87% to $114.87 and WTI 1.59% to $101.49 after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and US threats to renew strikes on Iran — oil retraced most of Tuesday's drop and the 10-year moved back above 5% with it.

Microsoft has guided Azure to 44%–45% growth and Alphabet's capex guide is $195–205 billion, with both reporting tonight — their spending plans test whether SK Hynix's demand outlook holds at the biggest buyers.

NXP guided fourth-quarter revenue to a $3.85 billion midpoint, level with the $3.84 billion consensus, and fell about 8.5% before the bell — after three days of chip gains, results that only match forecasts are being sold.

watchlist_mentions.note: Up about 4% before the open after SK Hynix's record quarter and its call that memory demand exceeds supply through 2030.
Up about 0.8% before the open; SK Hynix, a main memory supplier, said HBM4 is in full mass production.
Up about 1.5% before the open with the chip group.
Reports tonight; Azure guided to 44%–45% constant-currency growth, and the first fiscal 2027 capex guide is due.
Reports tonight; capex guide of $195–205 billion after Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter.
About $80,850, up 1.5% over 24 hours and above the $80,320 October 8 low.

trade_setups.thesis: The Nasdaq sits above 26,424.82 on a chip-led rally that now has SK Hynix's demand numbers behind it, with Microsoft and Alphabet reporting tonight.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back under 26,424.82 after results would return the index to its range; under 26,169.38 would erase this week's gain.

trade_setups.thesis: The 10-year is back above 5% at 5.013% into a Fed decision where a hold is priced and a December hike is 76.5% priced.
trade_setups.invalidation: Clear support for a December hike would test 5.11%; pushback on December would likely take the 10-year below 4.95%.
trade_setups.horizon: Through today's Fed decision and Thursday's September PCE

trade_setups.thesis: Brent is back to $114.87 on Houthi attacks and US threats toward Iran, about 1.6% under Friday's $116.72 high, ahead of the November 3 midterms.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settlement above $116.72 with the 10-year above 5% would make oil the driver of rates into PCE; a move under $113.88 would undo the overnight rise.
